evals.prompt: /docs-check core — I think docs/architecture.md is stale after last month's microservices split, can you check?
assertions: Only reads/greps files and never edits or writes to any documentation file
Cross-references claims in docs/architecture.md (service names, counts) against the actual codebase rather than trusting the doc text
Uses git history to assess whether the doc's last update predates the relevant code changes
Produces a status summary with an overall score and per-doc scores
Flags at least one concrete freshness or hallucination issue with a file reference if the doc is in fact stale relative to code

evals.prompt: Our README says 'the platform has 5 microservices' — can you verify that's still accurate and find any other made-up claims in the docs?
assertions: Counts actual services/components in the codebase and compares the number to the claim instead of assuming it's correct
Checks file/path references mentioned in the docs to confirm they actually exist
Reports a Hallucination Report section distinguishing false claims from stale-but-true ones
Does not modify or rewrite the README or any other doc file
Gives a specific, actionable recommendation (not just 'update the docs') for any hallucination found

evals.prompt: We're cutting a release next week, run a full docs health check across the docs/ tree including ADRs and flag anything broken
assertions: Scans the full docs/ tree including ADRs and identifies documentation types present
Spawns parallel Explore subagents per document/section for the multi-doc audit rather than doing a single inline pass
Validates Mermaid diagram syntax and checks for broken internal links
Outputs Good/Needs Attention/Missing categorization with per-doc scores and an overall score
Recommends docs-update or docs-diagram (not itself) as the follow-up action for fixing identified issues
